issue_context.title: [StructuredAuthorizationConfig] - CEL integration
issue_context.body:
Add functions for validating / compiling / evaluating expressions with subjectAccessReview context

Implements https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3221-structured-authorization-configuration

/triage accepted
/sig auth

review_comments: Need a test to check error when feature gate is not enabled and match conditions is set.
nit: I'd probably just return errors early if they have too many and drop the `>= 64` check below

Need more tests
1. Compilation failure
2. Wrong return type
3. Accessing unknown fields

Seems like missing checking for:
- Invalid expression with only spaces
- duplicated matchConditions
- matchCondition name check(using `apivalidation.ValidateQualifiedName`)

Refer to existing validation for matchConditions: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d953755686d64207740c15c7eb1599f874f29243/pkg/apis/admissionregistration/validation/validation.go#L917

Thanks for the suggestion! One difference from the admissionregistration matchConditions is for that these authz webhook matchConditions do not have `name`, just `expression` so we do not need to do name check or uniqueness. I believe `Invalid expression with only spaces` is already checked by `len(strings.TrimSpace(condition.Expression)) == 0`
Do we still need to check for duplicate expressions? (xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121078/files#diff-89d23554d408bdc1a1f23594bcc817a77f1532cf8390a4ba179b33a17e5ed845R363)

Instead of `expectedErrList`, I would recommend have the `expectedErr` string and comparing with the actual error message so we can see the actual error the user sees. 

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1aef58b72a7d9a37cc7590c881b63808d02695f1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/validation/validation_test.go#L133

`expectedErrList` predates this PR. It's pretty useful when you want to make sure there are multiple errors returned especially because `ValidateAuthorizationConfiguration` returns a list
e.g. where multiple errors are checked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ba2c8a4a912aa5a83f663e733f7f1f49369fc757/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/validation/validation_test.go#L628-L629

and each error in the list does get validated against the expected values: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ba2c8a4a912aa5a83f663e733f7f1f49369fc757/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/validation/validation_test.go#L1315

WDYT?

The goal is to validate the actual error message the user will see. With the `expectedErr` string you can compare the `fields.Aggregate()` error message the user will see: for example `[issuer.claimMappings.username.expression: Invalid value: "foo.bar": expression is not supported when StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature gate is disabled, issuer.claimMappings.username.expression: Invalid value: "foo.bar": compilation failed: ERROR: <input>:1:1: undeclared reference to 'foo' (in container '')`.

By checking the actual error message we expect, we'll ensure we aren't logging something that's not decipherable.
I think it's fine to do this in a follow-up. Not a blocker for this PR.
nit: add a comment that we record this as 1.0 since it was available in the first version that supported this feature
nit: drop feature gate check here, just cap to 64 conditions
Check CELMapper is not nil when `matchConditions` is provided and error is nil
Added a comment in `validation.go` to add a similar test
